newsitem.title: UK: UK's oil licensing round breaks EU law - Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: UK's oil licensing round breaks EU law - Greenpeace.

text.p: Environmental group Greenpeace said on Wednesday that Britain's 17th offshore oil licensing round is in breach of European law.

"The breach has occurred because the Government failed to ensure that full environmental impact assessments (EIAs) were carried out in the area prior to development and failed to ensure appropriate public consultation," Greenpeace said in a statement.
Greenpeace, along with the Marine Conservation Society and the Whale and Dolphin Conservation Society, on Wednesday made an official complaint to the European Commission.

"The joint complaint calls on the Commission to expedite their considerations to prevent unlawful licenses being issued. In addition, Greenpeace has called upon the U.K. Government to abandon the oil licensing process," the statement said.
A spokeswoman for Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said that nobody was immediately available for comment.
Last week the DTI announced that Greenpeace had bid against leading oil companies for all of the 22,000 square miles of Atlantic acreage available in the 17th licensing round.
Greenpeace said it was given a deadline of April 3 to address the DTI's concerns that its application failed to fulfil the oil drilling and production criteria of the license.

"(Greenpeace addressed these concerns) today by claiming that the only license that the DTI can lawfully issue is to Greenpeace, since it is the only application designed to carry out the sort of EIA studies that the Government and oil companies are failing to do," the statement said.
